units.title: Multi-AZ database reliability
units.body: Production relational workloads on Amazon RDS should prefer Multi-AZ deployments so a standby replica in another Availability Zone can take over after a primary failure. Single-AZ deployments keep storage and compute in one zone and therefore create a single point of failure for availability. Multi-AZ is about high availability and failover, not a substitute for read scaling (read replicas serve a different purpose).
teaching_points: Multi-AZ targets failover/HA; read replicas target read scale-out.
Application connection handling must tolerate brief failover reconnects.
Backup and restore remain necessary even with Multi-AZ.

units.title: IAM roles for compute access
units.body: EC2 and other compute should obtain AWS API credentials from an instance profile / IAM role rather than embedding long-term access keys in images or environment files. Role credentials are temporary and rotated by the platform. Policies attached to the role should follow least privilege, granting only the actions and resources the workload needs (for example S3 GetObject on a specific bucket prefix).
teaching_points: Prefer roles over long-term access keys on servers.
Least privilege still applies to role policies.
Shared responsibility: AWS secures the credential delivery mechanism; you design the policy.

units.title: Load balancing and target health
units.body: An Application Load Balancer distributes HTTP/HTTPS traffic across healthy targets such as EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Health checks remove failing targets from rotation. Combining Multi-AZ target placement with an ALB reduces the blast radius of a single instance or AZ issue for user-facing traffic.
teaching_points: Health checks drive traffic away from failed targets.
Multi-AZ targets improve availability under AZ impairment.
ALB decouples clients from individual instance lifecycles.

excerpts.title: High Availability
excerpts.summary: High availability designs reduce downtime. Production databases should consider Multi-AZ deployments.
teaching_points: Prefer Multi-AZ for production RDS workloads to improve availability via standby replication.
Single-AZ RDS introduces a single point of failure for production databases.

excerpts.title: IAM roles instead of long-term credentials
excerpts.summary: EC2 instances use IAM roles to access S3 instead of long-term credentials.
teaching_points: Prefer instance/profile roles over embedded access keys.
Least privilege still applies to role policies.

excerpts.title: Load balancing to compute
excerpts.summary: An Application Load Balancer routes traffic to EC2 targets.
teaching_points: Edge and load-balancer tiers decouple clients from instance lifecycle.
Health checks and Multi-AZ placement improve reliability.
